summary: convert-native's streamed KML reader (services/geo/geo/native_gis.py) now records the byte index of each
start, end and character-data event and feeds the KML (or the KMZ's document member) in chunks of 64 KiB.
After each chunk, when more than TAG_BOUND (1 MiB) has been fed since the last event, the read stops with
code tag_too_large through the existing _KmlStop path: written layers are abandoned and the whole file is
returned not_converted with the words 'A KML tag is larger than 1 MiB before it closes; the file was not
read further. The original is kept with its SHA-256.' Expat therefore never holds more than about
1 MiB + 64 KiB of an open start tag, attribute value, comment or tag that never closes.

decisions.D1: TAG_BOUND = 1 MiB checked after every fed chunk of at most 64 KiB; code tag_too_large; the lead's words.
decisions.D2: The reader's handlers, DTD/entity refusal, layers, notRead counts and PLACEMARK_BOUND are unchanged.

code.where: _KmlStop carries code and reason; convert_kml_file returns the stop's reason as the layer's words
code.stoppedLayerContract: The TS StoppedLayerSchema is strict (layer, ordinal, state, reason), so the officer sees the words; the code tag_too_large is held on the stop and asserted in the test. No TS contract was changed.

probes.result: converted, 1 feature: text events keep the index moving
not_converted, tag_too_large words: Expat holds a comment whole too

probes.input: start tag that never closes, 3 MiB (test_only)
